contract.whyThisMatters: Three consecutive independent visual re-grades left Module 2 at SERVICEABLE-NOT-PREMIUM (D20, carried to the founder). The founder has now supplied a visual direction and activated a bounded quality war. If the product cannot reach premium sports-business media on its flagship lesson, the co-primary emotional north star (students genuinely want more) is at risk regardless of how correct the economics is; if it reaches premium by exposing hidden information or adding reward chrome, it fails the primary north star. This wave establishes, with fresh evidence, whether premium is genuinely unmet and why, and freezes the reference-to-product contract before any pixel is built.
uncertainties: Whether a fresh independent visual reviewer, judging rendered browser state against the founder references at 1366x768 and 1920x1080, confirms VERIFIED-UNMET, and what the highest-leverage causes are.

Which reference decisions create a concrete product problem (pre-lock revenue projections and demand curve vs the blind-commit loop; 'Maximize Revenue' vs the two un-summable books; reward footer vs D4; fictional nav destinations; teacher projections/countdown that the model does not make).

contract.passCondition: All required evidence recorded; the second independent visual review has returned an explicit verdict with ranked causes; every reference element that conflicts with hidden information, the two books, D4, or teacher truth has an economic-truth ruling; the three kid baselines are on file; the analyst's reconciliation recommends proceeding to the Full House build under a frozen reference-to-product contract.
contract.repairCondition: The second review returns INSUFFICIENT-EVIDENCE, or the contract cannot be frozen because a reference decision's adaptation is disputed between the visual reviewer and economic truth — then hold a bounded meeting with independent pre-opinions and re-freeze.
contract.rollbackCondition: Baseline capture or review activity modifies product code or run state; then restore the wave-0 checkpoint and re-run the audit read-only.
contract.killCondition: The second independent review returns VERIFIED-MET at the current head with evidence the prior three re-grades were wrong — then the premium war is unnecessary and the program returns to the founder with that finding.

sections.direction: Module 2 is the ticket office on game day before doors (M1 is the Cap Room after). The arena is an instrument, not a backdrop: the drawn bowl renders only settled turnout; pre-lock it is dark, closed, or absent. Premium comes from place, one hero per state, and almost nothing else on screen - not from violet/Inter alone. 75/25 budget named exactly: B1 sellout/house fills (/play + /board), B2 Two Peaks (/board), B3 class results frame (/board), B4 synthesis close (/board) at full cinema; H1 lock settle -> doors about to open and H2 N5-vs-N1 counterfactual at ~40%. /play state-by-state feelings; reference objects mapped: sidebar -> desk rail (club, night pips, two books docked, PIN demoted), goal card -> accountability card (two books, never Maximize Revenue), stat row -> tonight's printed facts, result screen -> box score with TURNOUT as hero, arena panel -> the building as a fill readout, dials -> two physical instruments of unequal size, bell -> a world event. /board: headline -> evidence -> footnote rail on every frame; the per-night class results table is missing today. /teach: calm command, Director Rail, elapsed clock only. Full memo: DIRECTION.md.

data.label: Kid B (casual sports student) full-pass gameplay critique, M2L1 Full House
Night 1 pre-lock pricing screen, first look — hero $24 figure, dial, LOCK IT IN, no preview
Night 1 to Night 2 transition, VIEWPORT truth — Night 1's result (0 attendance, -$520,000) is entirely off-screen; only Night 2's fresh pricing card is visible
Same moment, fullPage companion — shows the buried NIGHT 1 HOW IT WENT card (CAME 0 of 19,800, KEPT -$520,000) roughly 700px below the fold
Night 2 to Night 3 transition, fullPage — second confirmation of the same buried-result pattern (sellout, 1,208 turned away, scrolled below Night 3's pricing card)
End-of-PLAY summary screen — the one genuinely glanceable result screen: five-row table, positive template for per-night results

sections.what-the-student-plays: Five nights of set-one-number-and-wait: a facts card, one big price dial anchored at the season-plan price ($24 of a $10-$120 range), a secondary event-spend stepper, a Night-4 upper-bowl toggle, and one dominant LOCK IT IN button behind a confirm guard. No pre-lock preview of any kind, confirmed absent on every night's screen ('No preview. Nothing on this screen tells you what tonight will make.'). Two non-summable books (CASH, RENEWALS) update in a compact header strip after each close. REVEAL/ADAPT/COUNTERFACTUAL/SYNTHESIS move to the class board with a stronger, more premium visual register (arena backdrop, one chart per frame, one punchline sentence) than the student's own device carries.
sections.biggest-failure: The just-closed night's result is buried below the fold behind the NEXT night's full pricing UI on the 1366x768 student viewport. Confirmed at Night1->2 (screens-kid-b/06-play-night1-RESULT.png viewport vs -FULL.png fullPage: 0 attendance / -$520,000 result card sits ~700px below the fold, hidden behind Night 2's fresh dial and its own LOCK IT IN button) and again at Night2->3 (09-play-night2-RESULT-FULL.png: a sellout with 1,208 turned away, likewise buried). This inverts the founder-preserved reference decision that 'the result is a separate, larger state than the decision' (VISUAL_REFERENCE_SPEC section 2). For a persona who reads little and acts on the first big number/button she sees, the experience->consequence->adaptation loop that is this lesson's entire spine can be played end to end without the student ever reading a single per-night result card on her own screen -- only the compact red/gold CASH and RENEWALS header numbers are guaranteed visible, which register as 'good/bad' but not 'why.'
sections.moment-by-moment-notes: Join flow is clean, one screen, one CTA. HOOK is ~259 words and Night 1's pre-lock screen adds ~170 more before the first LOCK IT IN (measured on raw text dumps) -- heavy for this persona, though the hero price figure and dial and CTA remain findable without reading, so the mechanic itself is operable. The recurring blue guidance paragraph explaining the season-plan anchor repeats verbatim every night; a skim-first reader who reads it once (or never) then habituates to skipping it, so the actual pricing rule is experienced as an unexplained pattern rather than a taught mechanic. Kid B's naive play (price near dial max Night 1 -> zero attendance -> overcorrect near dial floor Night 2 -> sellout with fans turned away -> repeat Night 1's exact price on Night 5, same card, same result: zero again) produced a real, attributable, replayable causal story -- but that story lived in result cards the persona would structurally miss per the biggest-failure above. The Night-4 bowl toggle (CLOSED/OPEN, $95,000 cost) is legible and operable without reading its caption -- a genuine strength. The end-of-PLAY five-row summary table (17-play-night5-RESULT-allnights.png) is the one screen in the whole PLAY phase a fast reader could parse in ten seconds and should be the template for every per-night result, not just the final one. Board frames in REVEAL/ADAPT/COUNTERFACTUAL/SYNTHESIS are visually strong and would likely carry this persona's engagement if she is watching the class screen, independent of her own device's flaws. This was a solo one-desk test session; the COUNTERFACTUAL 'did anybody charge less and make more' prompt has no positive cross-desk answer at n=1 -- NOT VERIFIED as a flaw at real class scale.
sections.required-repairs: (1) Reorder or resequence the per-night transition so the just-closed night's result renders as its own screen state fully inside the 1366x768 viewport before the next night's pricing dial and LOCK button become the dominant on-screen action -- currently the next decision sits above the previous consequence in scroll order, screens-kid-b/06-play-night1-RESULT.png vs -FULL.png. (2) Stop repeating the identical guidance paragraph verbatim every night; either compress after Night 1 or make it reference the student's own last result so a skim-first reader gets a second real chance to absorb the mechanic. (3) Use the end-of-play summary table's glanceable table format (17-play-night5-RESULT-allnights.png) as the design template for every individual night's result card, not only the final one. Not recommending changes to: the join flow, the single-hero-figure-plus-single-CTA pricing card structure, the blind-commitment discipline (verified absent preview on every pre-lock screen), the bowl toggle's legible state change, or the board's visual register in REVEAL/ADAPT/COUNTERFACTUAL/SYNTHESIS.

data.finding: For the casual/low-reading grade 5-6 student pairs-on-one-device persona, the current M2L1 Full House build should not ship to a real classroom as-is. Every per-night result card renders below the fold behind the next night's full pricing UI on a 1366x768 student viewport (confirmed at two consecutive night transitions), inverting the founder's own preserved reference decision that the consequence gets a separate, larger screen state than the decision. A fast, low-reading student can play all five nights end to end -- dial, LOCK IT IN, dial, LOCK IT IN -- without ever reading a single one of her own result cards, leaving the experience->consequence->adaptation loop that is this lesson's core promise dependent entirely on a compact header number and, later, the class board -- not on anything her own device reliably shows her at the moment it matters.
